title: feat(desktop): zoom and reposition the camera image to frame yourself in the bubble
body:
> **Stacked on #404** (Mirror image). It targets `feat/camera-bubble-mirror`. Merge #404 first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

## What this does

Adds manual **framing** to the camera settings, both on the Record page and in the capture panel. A "Framing" switch turns it on when you need it. While it is on, a zoom slider (100–300 %), a position pad (drag the dot, or use the arrow keys) and a Reset button control which part of the camera image fills the bubble. The values are saved. Turning the switch off shows the bubble exactly as before and keeps the values for next time.

## Why

The owner asked for this: "necesito poder encuadrar cuando necesite". There was no way to zoom in when you sit far from the camera, or to recenter yourself when you are off to one side.

## What changes for you

- **New setting `AppSettings.cameraBubble.framing` = `{ enabled, zoom, x, y }`, default off.** With it off, the bubble renders exactly as before: no transform, and the camera at 480 lines as today.
- **With framing on and zoomed in, the camera is asked for more lines** (480, 720 or 1080), so the zoom does not upscale a small image. Expect more camera CPU at 1080.
- **During a take the camera resolution is frozen.** Zoom and position still apply at once, but the stream is not reopened until the take ends, because reopening blinks the bubble and that blink would be recorded.

## What to review

1. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/camera-bubble.ts` — `framingTransform`.** It produces `scale(z) translate(-x·r, -y·r)`, followed by `scaleX(-1)` when mirrored, with `r = (z-1)/(2z)`. This keeps the image covering the bubble at every pan, and the flip comes last so panning moves what you see the same way whether or not the image is mirrored. Check that convention against the pad: dot right should show more of the right side of the image.
2. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/shared/camera-bubble.ts` — `cameraCaptureLines`.** It picks the smallest of 480, 720 or 1080 that is at least `size × 2 × zoom`. The `×2` assumes a Retina display. Decide whether the 1080 cap and the 400 ms settle in `use-camera-preview.ts` are right.
3. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/camera-bubble/camera-bubble.tsx` — `takeLines`.** The resolution freezes while `activity.active` is true. A zoom made mid-take therefore runs at the start-of-take resolution, which can look soft at 300 % until the take ends. That is the trade-off for never recording a blink.
4. **`apps/kaipu-record/src/renderer/src/features/camera-settings/camera-settings-fields.tsx` — the position pad.** It uses `role="slider"` with a 2D `aria-valuetext` ("Left 40%, up 20%"), because a plain group cannot carry a value text. Arrows move it by 0.1 and Shift by 0.25, and it is disabled at zoom 100 %.

**Safe to skim:** fixtures that only add `framing`, the i18n pairs, and the backlog doc section.

## Proof

| Criterion | What was done | How to check it | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Framing can be turned on and off | `SwitchRow` "Framing"; the bubble transform is applied only when it is enabled | Manual 1 | `camera-bubble.test.tsx` ("leaves the video untouched while framing is off" and "applies the zoom and pan…"). **Not verified in the app.** |
| Zoom and position | slider, pad and Reset write `framing`; `framingTransform` | Manual 2 | `camera-bubble.test.ts` (shared) and `camera-settings-fields.test.tsx` pass. **Not verified in the app.** |
| No blink in the recording when zooming mid-take | resolution frozen during a take | Manual 3 | "keeps the camera resolution while recording…" test, watched red before the fix |

## Decisions

- **Manual framing, not automatic.** Options: macOS Center Stage (needs a native module, and only works with compatible cameras), our own face tracking (constant CPU, an experimental API), or manual. The owner chose manual; the other two stay open for later.
- **A position pad, not dragging inside the bubble.** Dragging the bubble already moves its window, so a second meaning for the same gesture would be ambiguous.
- **The resolution is frozen during a take** (see review item 3).
- **Reset keeps framing on**, and only recenters and sets zoom to 100 %.

## Checks

From `apps/kaipu-record` on this branch:

- `vitest run` → exit 0, 298 files, 2859 tests
- `bun run check-types` → exit 0
- `bun run lint` → exit 0, 0 errors, 17 warnings (same count as before)
- `packages/i18n` tests → exit 0, 22 tests
- `oxfmt --check` on the 17 changed files → exit 0

## Verify it yourself

**Setup:** `git switch feat/camera-bubble-framing && bun install && bun run dev`, then turn the camera on.

**1. Toggle.** In the camera settings, turn "Framing" on, set the zoom to 200 %, then turn Framing off.
Expect: the bubble zooms in, and with Framing off it looks exactly as it did before this PR.
Broken if: the bubble keeps the zoom after Framing is switched off.

**2. Zoom and position.** Set the zoom to 200 % and drag the dot to the right; then press ← a few times; then Reset.
Expect: dragging right shows more of the right side of the image, and the bubble never shows empty edges. With Mirror on or off, dot right still shows more of the right of what you see. Reset recenters and sets 100 %.
Broken if: a direction is reversed with Mirror on, or empty edges appear.

**3. Mid-take.** Start a recording and change the zoom from 100 % to 250 % during it.
Expect: the zoom applies with no blink in the exported video. It may look a little soft until the take ends.
Broken if: the export shows the bubble blinking or blank for a moment.

**4. Sharpness.** With the take stopped and the zoom at 250 %, wait a second.
Expect: the image sharpens, because the camera reopens at a higher resolution.

## Manual verification

- [ ] Step 1: the toggle on and off
- [ ] Step 2: pan direction with Mirror on and off; no empty edges
- [ ] Step 3: no blink in the export
- [ ] Step 4: sharper after the take
- [ ] The pad's look in the capture panel (80 px) and on the Record page
- [ ] Camera CPU at 1080 lines is acceptable

## What I did not verify

- Nothing was run in the Electron app or with a real camera, including iPhone Continuity Camera.
- Whether pan and zoom feel right in a circle compared with a rounded square; the pad ignores the bubble's shape.
- CPU and heat at 1080 lines.
